summary: Office refrigerator temperature sensor floods monitoring with alerts
description: Issue summary: Starting 2025-11-12 01:45 UTC, the office refrigerator temperature sensor (vendor-controller v2.3) began emitting intermittent high-temperature alerts to the central monitoring stack. Impact: noisy alert flood for the monitoring team and multiple on-call escalations; no customer-facing impact. Environment: on-prem office network, SNMP exporter on office gateway (10.1.3.1), Prometheus scrape interval 15s, alert rule fridge_temp_high > 8C for 3m. Steps to reproduce: 1) Observe Prometheus alert stream between 01:30-03:00 UTC; 2) Check sensor telemetry via SNMP; 3) Correlate with gateway syslog. Logs/snippets: several telemetry entries show temperature values of "NaN" or spikes to 999.9 followed by normal readings. Investigation notes: initial hypothesis is flaky SNMP exporter or controller firmware regression after scheduled firmware update on 2025-11-11. Facilities team reports the controller shows intermittent packet loss. Workaround: suppressed the specific alert group to reduce on-call noise and added a short-term mute on the rule. Proposed remediation: schedule an office controller power-cycle and open a vendor RMA if issue recurs; consider throttling rule to ignore single-sample spikes.
comments: Priya Nair (Support): We received ~120 alerts from the fridge alert rule between 01:45-02:30. Pager went off repeatedly. I've attached the alert digests to the ticket.

Evan Chen (SRE): Looking at the gateway exporter logs, I'm seeing repeated SNMP timeouts coincident with the spikes. Possible firmware regression on the controller side. Can facilities power-cycle the controller and monitor?
Lena Park (Reporter): Logs uploaded to shared drive: https://drive.redwood.internal/office-fridge-logs-20251112. Note several readings labeled 'NaN' and occasional 999.9 values.
Samir Patel (Facilities): I'll do a power-cycle at 2025-11-14 09:00 PT and report back. We can also move the controller to a spare port on the gateway to rule out cabling.

Evan Chen (SRE): After the power-cycle, alerts dropped off for ~18 hours. Leaving open to observe; recommend replacing controller if we see a recurrence. Also propose adding a small Prometheus recording rule to smooth transient spikes.
Priya Nair (Support): Confirming suppression kept on during low-confidence period; will update runbook if vendor confirms firmware bug.
resolution_notes: Temporary: suppressed noisy alert group and power-cycled controller. Follow-up: facilities to monitor for recurrence and file vendor RMA if similar behavior within 7 days.
